overview: Implementation study of a service-wide triage and queue protocol on a regional crisis text line, using platform logs for an interrupted time series (52 weeks before and 26 weeks after go-live) and RE-AIM delivery and acceptance measures.
population: All conversations opened on the line from 12 January 2026 to 11 July 2027; evening shifts (18:00 to 24:00) for the primary outcome; all volunteer responders active after go-live for acceptance measures.
exposure: The protocol from 11 January 2027: automated acknowledgement within 30 seconds, keyword flag moving high-risk messages to the front of the queue, and a surge roster triggered when more than 10 texters are waiting.
procedures: Once the agreement is signed, the vendor exports de-identified conversation records (open time, first automated reply, first human reply, close or abandonment time, flag time, queue length, counsellor log-in times) without message text. The agency's data lead builds weekly series. Volunteers complete a four-item acceptability scale at weeks 8 and 24 (under 5 minutes each). Fidelity is computed from queue order and log-in times.

outcomes.name: Time to first human reply in evening shifts
outcomes.measure: Weekly median minutes from conversation open to first human reply, 18:00 to 24:00
outcomes.timing: Weekly, 52 weeks before and 26 weeks after go-live
outcomes.why: The wait texters experience at the worst moment.

outcomes.name: Abandoned conversations
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of conversations closed by the texter before a human reply
outcomes.why: People who give up waiting receive no help.

outcomes.name: Flag fidelity
outcomes.measure: Proportion of queue episodes in which flagged messages were answered before earlier unflagged messages

outcomes.name: Surge roster response
outcomes.measure: Proportion of surge triggers with a counsellor logged in within 10 minutes
outcomes.why: Capacity arrives only if counsellors log in.

outcomes.name: Counsellor overtime
outcomes.measure: Hours of on-call time per week beyond rostered hours
outcomes.why: The surge roster must not burn out paid staff.

feasibility: Uses existing logs and staff time; volunteer time is under 10 minutes over six months; the whole analysis waits on the vendor agreement.
biasMitigation: Fifty-two pre-implementation weeks to model trend and season
Weekly demand (conversations opened) as a covariate
Outcome definitions fixed before the vendor export
Fidelity computed from system timestamps, not self-report

biasFlags.label: Co-interventions and demand shifts
biasFlags.note: Media events or school terms change demand; annotated and modelled.

biasFlags.label: Timestamp definitions
biasFlags.note: Automated and human replies must be separated in the export.

biasFlags.label: Volunteer response bias
biasFlags.note: Acceptability may be rated by the most engaged volunteers.

flags: Covariates limited to demand, season and holiday weeks
parsimony.simplestPath: One weekly service outcome in a time series plus two fidelity proportions.

theoreticalFramework: RE-AIM for reach, adoption, implementation and maintenance; no additional determinant framework until fidelity data show where delivery fails.
summary: Interrupted time series with one primary outcome, one secondary, two fidelity measures and one balancing measure, gated on the vendor agreement.
